HEATHER BOUCHARD

CCC Peer / The Sensory Regulation System

Profile Data
  • Major: Nuclear Medicine
  • Status: Disconnected
  • Role: The Safe Person / The Rescuer
  • Physical Parameters: Deep Pressure Hugs Only

The Rescuer Protocol

Following a catastrophic "Unhandled Exception"—an abusive relationship that Matt barely survived prior to meeting her—Heather was the one who initiated the recovery protocol. She picked him up, dusted him off, and fundamentally decided he was worth something, re-establishing his baseline value when his systems were completely compromised.

The Sensory Regulation System

Heather did not function as a traditional romantic interest; she operated as a vital "Sensory Regulation System." Around her, Matt was able to safely power down his neurodivergent "masking" subroutines. She provided an incredibly safe, judgment-free environment where he was accepted without pity or awkwardness.

The Concrete Parameters

Their connection was built on rigid, concrete physical and geographic boundaries that Matt's logical brain found deeply comforting. Physically, she allowed "Best Friend Hugs" that provided essential deep-pressure grounding, while strictly restricting hand-holding or kissing. Geographically, she maintained a "Boolean Boundary" by politely declining invitations to the Kids House, keeping their relationship cleanly isolated to the CCC campus.

The Silent Overload

Unlike a malicious antagonist, Heather’s ultimate failure stemmed from her own unarticulated neurological limits. Balancing the grueling demands of her Nuclear Medicine track with the high-engagement social routine of the CCC cafeteria slowly drained her processing RAM. Lacking the emotional vocabulary to request a temporary pause, her brain defaulted to its only fail-safe: completely deleting the variable. Her sudden, silent departure on the CTS bus stripped away Matt's primary safety net, causing a catastrophic system crash and leaving behind a permanent Syntax Error that his mind could never logically resolve.

The Modern Reflection

Looking back at the early 2000s, Matt explicitly considers Heather to have been his closest friend during that deeply formative era. If asked today to compress the complexity of his lingering grief and the catastrophic nature of that sudden departure into audio, the answer lies in the 2002 Crimson Node debut album. The devastating, frantic track Unhandled Exception perfectly encapsulates the sudden, silent system crash, while the upbeat synth-pop paradox of Paired Devices captures the profound isolation of navigating the aftermath alone.
